beats.text: One order, three databases. One fails halfway...
beats.say: Placing one order has to update three databases: orders, payments, and inventory. What if one of them fails halfway?

beats.text: All succeed, or all fail: with a coordinator.
beats.say: Two-phase commit makes them all succeed, or all fail, using a coordinator.

beats.text: Phase 1: prepare. Can you commit? Vote yes or no.
beats.say: Phase one: prepare. The coordinator asks every participant, can you commit? Each one saves the change safely, and votes yes or no.
If everyone votes yes, phase two begins. The coordinator tells all of them to commit.

beats.text: One no? Everyone rolls back. All or nothing.
beats.say: But if even one votes no, the coordinator tells everyone to roll back. All or nothing.

beats.text: The catch: if the coordinator dies, everyone blocks.
beats.say: The catch: if the coordinator crashes after the votes, participants are stuck waiting, holding their locks. That's why two-phase commit can block.
